en: Storing raw meat on the refrigerator's bottom shelf prevents its liquid juices from dripping onto and contaminating ready-to-eat foods below.
Shaking an oil and vinegar dressing temporarily creates a suspension, but the oil quickly separates and floats because it is less dense.
Mixing household bleach and vinegar produces toxic chlorine gas, so you must never combine these two liquid cleaning products.
Chewing food thoroughly increases its surface area, helping saliva chemically break down starches faster for better digestion.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes protects you from electric shocks because rubber is an electrical insulator that stops current from flowing.
Sweating cools your body because liquid water on your skin absorbs body heat to evaporate into water vapor.
Filtering tap water through an activated carbon pitcher removes harmful impurities because the porous charcoal traps solid particles and chemicals.
Leaving a wet iron bicycle chain exposed to oxygen and moisture causes rusting, a chemical change that weakens the metal.
Wearing a light-colored cotton shirt keeps you cooler in the sun because light colors reflect heat and cotton absorbs sweat.
Dissolving oral rehydration salts in clean water creates a solution that helps your intestines absorb fluids faster during diarrhea.
Using a wooden spoon to stir boiling soup prevents burns because wood is a thermal insulator that conducts heat poorly.
Storing medicines in a cool, dark cabinet prevents chemical degradation, ensuring the pills remain safe and effective to consume.
